waiting.title: The shop is findable now, and still nobody buys
waiting.body: Three page-one positions on Etsy AU, read logged out: second for dementia caregiver binder, fourth for caregiver binder printable, ninth for aging parent care planner. Forty-six listings live, zero sales ever. Ranking is not a visit, and a visit is not a sale. So the unproven part has moved to what happens AFTER someone sees the listing - the thumbnail and the first two lines of the title. Do not answer this with a forty-seventh product.

waiting.title: Your seven passwords live on one computer only
waiting.body: OpenAI, Gemini, Apify, Notion, Groq and Cerebras keys sit in one file on the Mac that is deliberately never backed up. Lose that machine and they are gone - about an hour to re-issue them all. Putting them in your password manager costs you five minutes.

waiting.tag: Asked 7 Sep, half solved by itself
waiting.title: The old project folder is still inside iCloud, with a duplicate beside it
waiting.body: The work now has a copy outside iCloud, so the danger is smaller than it was. But the Desktop copy is still there, and sitting next to it this morning is a second folder whose name ends in the number two - which is exactly what iCloud makes when it cannot decide which version is real. Deciding which one is the real folder, and deleting the other, is yours.

waiting.tag: Live on your shop right now
waiting.title: Thirteen live listing images have unreadable hairline text
waiting.body: The Caregiver Binder images fell back to a bitmap font that ignored the size it was given, so the text printed about ten pixels tall. Nothing errored, which is why it shipped. The code is fixed and the images are rebuilt - replacing pictures on live listings is yours. Nobody has re-checked this since the sixth.

waiting.tag: They disagreed, so it is yours
waiting.title: Etsy Plus - keep it or cancel it
waiting.body: The two AIs split on this, so it comes to you. There is also three dollars eighty of unused ads credit sitting on the account, which only became visible once the campaign stopped.

waiting.title: Kawaii Bunny says 25 pages; a 24-page rebuild is sitting unpublished
waiting.body: The rebuild was made because a measuring tool was wrong - and the tool was wrong, not the book. So the rebuild is no longer an improvement. Either keep serving the twenty-five page file, or upload the rebuild and edit the description in the same action. Never one without the other.

waiting.tag: It runs, but not every morning
waiting.title: The daily paper missed two of the last three mornings
waiting.body: There was an edition on the tenth and a catch-up on the twelfth. Nothing ran on the eleventh, and the twelfth's own file says its six a.m. run produced nothing either, so a person had to start it by hand. A brief that is not there when you wake up is not a brief. Worth deciding whether it gets fixed or dropped.

blocked.tag: Waiting on Amazon, not on you
blocked.title: Amazon still says your maze book contains no AI content
blocked.body: It should read yes, for text and images. You authorised the fix in writing on 4 September. It has not been done because Amazon has the book locked - the edit pages bounce straight back to the shelf, and the menu offers only add to series and archive. Checked again on 10 September, six days after review cleared.

news.title: AFR — Saturday 12 September 2026
news.caveat: This edition covers two days, not one. The six a.m. run produced nothing on the eleventh, so this is the catch-up job: nineteen new stories from the eleventh and twelfth.

stories.h: The one to read twice: a US rate rise next week is now close to certain
stories.p: Three separate stories in this edition all point the same way. When rates go up, households usually tighten on small extras a few weeks later, not the same day.
pts: US inflation came in hotter than expected, which makes a rise more likely.
Wall Street rose anyway, with the rise all but priced in already.
A columnist warns markets are ignoring a real inflation risk from rising energy prices.
What it means for you: watch your shop traffic over the next month rather than reacting to this today.

stories.h: Oil hit a five-month high as Middle East attacks disrupt shipping
stories.p: Oil this high eventually feeds into paper, printing and shipping costs.
pts: That reaches your Amazon paperback, because somebody has to print and post it.
It does not touch the digital files at all. Nothing is printed and nothing is shipped.
A major Australian-run fund lost another ten billion dollars as investors left the region.

stories.h: The housing slump is deepening, and the bond market is making it worse
stories.p: A deepening housing slump tends to show up a few weeks later as households trimming what they spend on small things, including small online purchases.
pts: The Australian share market fell for a fourth session in a row.
A lender is selling a hundred and sixty-two homes and land lots after a developer collapsed.
What it means for you: worth watching shop traffic against this, not worth changing anything yet.

stories.h: Rising borrowing costs are blowing a ten billion dollar hole in government budgets
stories.p: When governments start tightening under pressure like this, consumer confidence usually softens with it.
pts: The Treasurer also backed off a planned cap on tax breaks for start-up investors.
The Victorian Coalition says it would scrap a two billion dollar state venture fund.
A useful backdrop if your shop looks quiet over the next month or two.

stories.h: A hostile takeover fight over a tutoring company is picking up steam
stories.p: Education and learning products still attract real investor money.
pts: Worksheets and learning printables sit in a category buyers keep paying for.
That is the one genuinely encouraging line in this edition for what you sell.

stories.h: An Australian maths professor is publicly fighting OpenAI over a claimed breakthrough
stories.p: Even OpenAI's own claim about what its AI solved is being challenged in public.
pts: The same discipline applies closer to home. Only claim what a tool actually did.
That goes for a listing description and for an AI disclosure alike.
A cabinet minister accused Pauline Hanson of doing a billionaire's bidding, and a Liberal member is trying to turn her from underdog into villain.
Labor is planning new sanctions on Israel but resisting pressure for a full trade ban.
London could add a five per cent tourist tax to hotel and short-stay bookings.
German police say they foiled a planned attack, and a very large British political donation is drawing scrutiny.
